hunks.baseline: Traveling with the Zhongnan Sect was decided all of a sudden.
hunks.sol: We ended up traveling with the Zhongnan Sect almost before I knew it.

hunks.baseline: Their Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, had proposed joining forces, and Jeok Cheongang had accepted before I could finish thinking it over.
hunks.sol: Their Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, proposed it, and while I was still thinking it over, Jeok Cheongang cut in and accepted.

hunks.baseline: “Traveling together, huh? That’s not a bad idea.”
hunks.sol: “Traveling together? That wouldn’t be a bad idea.”

hunks.baseline: “What are you standing around for? Get your subordinates ready. And you too, Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord—start by kicking those lazy disciples of yours in the ass.”
hunks.sol: “What are you waiting for? Get your men ready. And you, Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord—start by kicking those disciples of yours off their asses.”

hunks.baseline: Just like that, all the preparations were finished in the blink of an eye.
hunks.sol: Just like that, the preparations were over.

hunks.baseline: Our party had swelled to around a thousand, rounding up a bit, and we set off toward Gansu. Among them were the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword, neither of whom looked particularly pleased.
hunks.sol: Our party, now a little over a thousand if I rounded generously, set off toward Gansu. The Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword came along too, neither looking pleased about it.

hunks.baseline: “Those two have looked like they’re on their deathbeds for a while now. If we’d met them just six months earlier, no more, no less, I’d have cracked them across the jaw first thing.”
hunks.sol: “Those two have had faces like thunder for a while now. If we’d met even six months earlier, I’d have punched them in the jaw first thing.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang smacked his lips as he muttered, and I clicked my tongue softly.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang smacked his lips. I clicked my tongue.

hunks.baseline: “If you couldn’t stand the sight of them, you shouldn’t have accepted the offer.”
hunks.sol: “If you didn’t want to look at them, you shouldn’t have accepted.”

hunks.baseline: “Is that why your lips are sticking out three inches?”
hunks.sol: “Is that why your lips are sticking out three feet?”

hunks.baseline: “Who said my lips were sticking out?”
hunks.sol: “Who says my lips are sticking out?”

hunks.baseline: “Correction. They’re sticking out four inches now.”
hunks.sol: “Correction. Four feet now.”

hunks.baseline: I shook my head at Jeok Cheongang’s teasing.
hunks.sol: I shook my head at his teasing.

hunks.baseline: The one small upside was that we’d taken the rear, keeping a good thirty jang between us and the Zhongnan Sect. At least we could have this conversation without everyone hearing.
hunks.sol: We’d taken the rear, a good thirty jang behind the Zhongnan Sect. Being far enough away to talk openly was about the only advantage I could see.

hunks.baseline: “Yes, I’m annoyed. Happy now?”
hunks.sol: “Yes, I’m annoyed. Happy?”

hunks.baseline: “Honestly, I can’t make heads or tails of you. If that’s how you feel, why bother making up when it was nothing but an empty gesture?”
hunks.sol: “I can never quite figure you out. Why make up with them if it was only for show?”

hunks.baseline: An empty gesture.
hunks.sol: Only for show.

hunks.baseline: There was no more and no less to it. It was exactly the right way to put it.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t have put it better myself.

hunks.baseline: I’d already guessed that Jeok Cheongang had heard everything that had passed between us through Sound Transmission, so I answered without much surprise.
hunks.sol: I’d already guessed Jeok Cheongang had heard everything we’d said through Sound Transmission, so I answered without surprise.

hunks.baseline: “Because we need to?”
hunks.sol: “Because you need to?”

hunks.baseline: “Right.”
hunks.sol: “Yes.”

hunks.baseline: “You make peace because you need to, then cover up old grudges with smiles, at least on the surface… You’ve grown up, haven’t you?”
hunks.sol: “You make peace because you need to, and smile as if the old grudges are behind you… You’ve grown up.”

hunks.baseline: Not sure whether Jeok Cheongang was praising me or scolding me, I stared at him in silence. He gave a quiet laugh.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t tell whether that was praise or a rebuke. When I stared at him without answering, he gave a quiet laugh.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t overthink it. I’m just glad to see you’ve grown in one direction or another.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t overthink it. I’m glad to see you’ve grown, whichever direction it may be in.”

hunks.baseline: “Do you think the direction you mentioned might be the wrong one?”
hunks.sol: “Do you think it might be the wrong direction?”

hunks.baseline: “Who can say? What matters is the outcome, doesn’t it?”
hunks.sol: “Who knows? What matters is the outcome.”

hunks.baseline: “Isn’t the process usually considered just as important as the outcome? Sometimes more important?”
hunks.sol: “Don’t people usually say the process matters just as much? Sometimes more?”

hunks.baseline: “The first is what people say when they’re narrow-minded, and the second is bullshit people use when they’ve completely botched the outcome.”
hunks.sol: “The first is what narrow-minded fools say. The second is bullshit from people who’ve thoroughly botched the outcome.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang answered with cutting certainty, then went on.
hunks.sol: Having delivered that verdict without a trace of hesitation, Jeok Cheongang continued.

hunks.baseline: “If I thought you’d done something wrong, I’d have given you a proper scolding. But so far, you haven’t done too badly. Besides, it might be nice to herd those lazy bastards all the way to Gansu like cattle.”
hunks.sol: “If I thought you’d done wrong, I’d have given you a proper scolding. So far, though, you haven’t done too badly. Besides, driving those lazy bastards all the way to Gansu like cattle has its appeal.”

hunks.baseline: He wasn’t wrong. Even now, the Zhongnan Sect Disciples were running for their lives. It was all because of what Jeok Cheongang had declared before we set out, after unilaterally claiming the rear.
hunks.sol: He wasn’t wrong. Even now, the Zhongnan Sect Disciples were running their asses off, thanks to the declaration Jeok Cheongang had made before we set out and he’d claimed the rear for himself.

hunks.baseline: “From this moment until we reach Gansu, if any of you fall behind or try to slack off, this old man will personally have a private talk with you.”
hunks.sol: “From now until we reach Gansu, anyone who falls even a little behind or tries to slack off gets a private meeting with this old man.”

hunks.baseline: A private lesson with an elder who’d reached a distant realm would be a fortuitous encounter anyone would pray for—unless the teacher was the Fire King. In that case, there was a good chance you’d become a dead man.
hunks.sol: A private meeting with a venerable master who’d reached an unfathomable realm would be a fortuitous encounter anyone might wish for. If that master was the Fire King, though, there was a good chance you’d be the one people called “the late.”

hunks.baseline: Have you ever seen a pack of hyenas—or rather, Zhongnan Sect Disciples—race for their lives along a mountainside, desperate to survive?
hunks.sol: Have you ever seen hyenas racing for their lives along a mountainside? Or rather, Zhongnan Sect Disciples?

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang watched with satisfaction as the Zhongnan Sect Disciples ran with every last bit of strength they could squeeze out. Then, without warning, he kicked off the ground.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang watched them sprint with every last bit of strength they had, looking thoroughly satisfied. Then he suddenly kicked off the ground.

hunks.baseline: A sharp boom rang out as his figure stretched away in an instant.
hunks.sol: A sharp boom rang out. His figure shot forward, leaving an afterimage behind.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang’s afterimage seemed to remain behind as he rapidly closed in. The Zhongnan Sect Disciples sucked in their breath, and panicked shouts rang out among them.
hunks.sol: The Zhongnan Sect Disciples saw him closing in, sucked in their breath, and began shouting.

hunks.baseline: “S-Senior Brother, I can’t go on. Don’t worry about this useless Junior Brother—just go on without me…”
hunks.sol: “S-Senior Brother, I can’t go on. Don’t worry about this useless Junior Brother. Just go…”

hunks.baseline: “No! Don’t give up! We can survive!”
hunks.sol: “No! Don’t give up! You can make it!”

hunks.baseline: My thoughts on the scene were short and clear.
hunks.sol: My thoughts on the scene were brief.

hunks.baseline: You’re all making a damn spectacle of yourselves.
hunks.sol: What the hell is wrong with you people?

hunks.baseline: I clicked my tongue at the Zhongnan Sect Disciples fleeing like locusts from a wildfire. Then I spotted something and narrowed my eyes.
hunks.sol: I was clicking my tongue at the Zhongnan Sect Disciples fleeing like locusts from a wildfire when I spotted something and narrowed my eyes.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, I realized the real reason Jeok Cheongang had suddenly sped ahead.
hunks.sol: Then I understood why Jeok Cheongang had suddenly sped ahead.

hunks.baseline: We emerged from the narrow mountain path, and a hill opened up the view.
The problem was that, at the same time, a small village appeared in the distance, its hundred or so thatched cottages huddled together—and a crowd of people gathered around it.
hunks.sol: We had come out of the narrow mountain path, and a hill opened up the view ahead. In the distance stood a small village, its hundred or so thatched cottages huddled together. A crowd had gathered around it.

hunks.baseline: At a glance, there had to be several hundred of them.
hunks.sol: There had to be several hundred people.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin, who’d spotted the crowd milling around the entrance to the little village a moment later, widened his eyes.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin spotted the crowd at the village entrance a moment after I did. His eyes widened.

hunks.baseline: His urgent voice reached my ears.
Guessing what he was about to say, I answered a beat ahead of him.
“Don’t panic already. They don’t look like enemies.”
hunks.sol: I could hear the urgency in his voice. Before he could finish, I said, “Don’t panic. They don’t look like enemies.”

hunks.baseline: I gave him a brief answer, thought for a moment, then added,
“At least, from what we can see right now.”
hunks.sol: I thought for a moment and added, “At least, from what I can see.”

hunks.baseline: I added that because I wasn’t completely sure myself.
Judging by the route we’d taken, we were now somewhere along the border between Shaanxi and Gansu.

hunks.sol: I wasn’t completely sure. Judging by our route, we were somewhere on the border between Shaanxi and Gansu. Dark Heaven had the dark art known as the Moving Formation, so running into its people disguised as civilians here wouldn’t be all that surprising.

hunks.baseline: Dark Heaven had already disguised its people as government troops in Sichuan once before.
hunks.sol: They’d already disguised themselves as government troops in Sichuan once.

hunks.baseline: *If something had happened in Gansu, word would’ve reached us by now. So what’s this crowd doing in a tiny mountain village? Are they really preparing an ambush using a Moving Formation?*
hunks.sol: *If something had happened in Gansu, word would’ve reached us by now. So what are that many people doing in a tiny mountain village? Is Dark Heaven preparing an ambush with a Moving Formation?*

hunks.baseline: Questions chased one another through my mind.
hunks.sol: One question led to another.

hunks.baseline: Then, all of a sudden, I heard a chilling sound.
I turned and saw Sama Pyo. He’d drawn the Black Dragon Saber, the weapon that shared its name with his sobriquet.
hunks.sol: At the sudden sound of a blade being drawn, I turned. Sama Pyo had drawn the Black Dragon Saber, the weapon that shared its name with his sobriquet.

hunks.baseline: “Whatever they are, there’s no harm in being prepared, is there, Pavilion Master?”
hunks.sol: “Whoever they are, it won’t hurt to be prepared. Wouldn’t you agree, Pavilion Master?”

hunks.baseline: His voice was calm, but his eyes were dark and intent.
hunks.sol: His voice was calm, but his eyes had gone dark. The closer we got to Gansu, the heavier the air around him had become.

hunks.baseline: The closer we got to Gansu, the heavier the atmosphere around Sama Pyo had become. I quietly nodded and urged my horse on.
hunks.sol: I nodded and urged my horse on.

hunks.baseline: My grassland horse’s hooves thundered across the ground.
hunks.sol: My grassland horse’s hooves pounded the ground.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know who the crowd waiting ahead of us really was, but one thing was certain.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know who the people ahead of us were, but I was sure of one thing.

hunks.baseline: *Even if Dark Heaven prepared an ambush, all we have to do is trample them and keep going.*
hunks.sol: *Even if this is Dark Heaven’s ambush, we can trample them and keep going.*

hunks.baseline: We might be headed into a fierce battle, but my heartbeat was no different from usual.
hunks.sol: We might be riding into a fierce battle. My heartbeat didn’t change.

hunks.baseline: I’d become far too strong to be stopped in some mountain valley like this.
hunks.sol: I’d grown far too strong to be stopped in a mountain valley like this.

hunks.baseline: No—I should correct that.
hunks.sol: No. Let me correct that.

hunks.baseline: It would be much more accurate to say that, at least for our side, it didn’t.
hunks.sol: It never happened to our side.

hunks.baseline: “They’re here! They’ve shown up!”
hunks.sol: “They’re here! Those bastards are here!”

hunks.baseline: It was only natural that urgent shouts and screams erupted all around us.
hunks.sol: The shouts and screams were only natural. Close to a thousand suspicious people had come pouring over the steep hill like water through a broken embankment, and some already had blades in their hands.

hunks.baseline: Nearly a thousand suspicious people came pouring over the steep hill, like water bursting through a broken embankment. Some of them already had gleaming blades in their hands. To the hundreds gathered around the entrance to the little village, it must have looked like a catastrophe.
hunks.sol: To the hundreds gathered at the little village entrance, it must have looked like a catastrophe.

hunks.baseline: At their very real reaction, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, racing at the head of the group alongside Jeok Cheongang, shouted like a thunderclap.
hunks.sol: Their terror was impossible to fake. The Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, racing at the front alongside Jeok Cheongang, shouted like thunder.

hunks.baseline: It was an order from none other than the Sect Leader.
hunks.sol: It was an order from the Sect Leader himself. His voice carried internal energy, and the Zhongnan Sect Disciples quickly slowed to a halt.

hunks.baseline: At his shout, reinforced with internal energy, countless Zhongnan Sect Disciples quickly slowed and stopped where they were. But there were always exceptions.
hunks.sol: But there are always exceptions.

hunks.sol: Two figures kept shooting forward like the wind, ignoring the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s command. I’d been slowing with the Zhongnan Sect Disciples, but at the sight of their backs, I clicked my tongue to myself.

hunks.baseline: *Yeah. Somehow I knew they’d do that.*
hunks.sol: *Yeah. I had a feeling they’d do that.*

hunks.baseline: They say old habits die hard for a reason.
hunks.sol: Old habits die hard.

hunks.baseline: Those two old dogs kept going, disregarding the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord’s orders because he was their Junior Brother, Sect Leader or not. I kicked off the ground after them.
hunks.sol: Sect Leader or not, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord was their Junior Brother. Those two old dogs ignored his order and kept going.
I kicked off the ground after them.

hunks.baseline: A gale wrapped around me, and I covered dozens of jang in a single instant.
hunks.sol: A gale wrapped around me as I crossed dozens of jang in an instant. The two old Daoists drew closer. So did the civilians’ screams.

hunks.baseline: The backs of the two old Daoists, who hadn’t slowed their pace, came closer. So did the civilians’ screams.

hunks.baseline: And right then, one person’s voice reached the ears of everyone there, including me.
hunks.sol: Then a voice reached every ear, including mine.

hunks.baseline: It was a low voice, neither shouted with force nor backed by any particular internal energy.
hunks.sol: It was quiet—not a forceful shout, and it carried no particular internal energy.

hunks.baseline: But that one word was enough to stop the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword in their tracks.
hunks.sol: One word was enough to stop the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword in their tracks. More important than the word itself was the man who’d said it.

hunks.baseline: More than anything, what mattered wasn’t what the word meant. It was who had said it.
“Are you deaf? You look useless enough already. Want me to rip one of your ears off while I’m at it?”
hunks.sol: “Are you deaf? Those ears don’t seem much use. Want me to rip one off?”

hunks.baseline: The Roaring Fury Swordsman had stopped only a few steps away from a civilian who stood frozen with his eyes squeezed shut. His face stiff, he began to speak.
hunks.sol: The Roaring Fury Swordsman had stopped only a few steps from a civilian whose eyes were squeezed shut. Looking uneasy, he said, “Senior Jeok. I only wanted to check…”

hunks.baseline: “Senior, I was only trying to make sure…”

hunks.baseline: “Answer what I asked. Should I take it off or not?”
hunks.sol: “Answer the question. Should I rip it off or not?”

hunks.baseline: “I thought you were just deaf, but now it looks like your mouth’s been sealed shut too. Fine. You answer for your Senior Brother, who can’t manage it himself.”
hunks.sol: “I thought you were just deaf, but now it seems your mouth doesn’t work either. Fine. You answer for your Senior Brother, since he’s having trouble.”

hunks.baseline: Fire flickered in Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.

hunks.sol: Fire flickered in Jeok Cheongang’s eyes. The Taeeul Merciless Sword met his gaze and bowed his head slightly.

hunks.baseline: “I only wanted to confirm who they were. I had no other intention. If my rash action upset you, Great Hero Jeok…”
hunks.sol: “We only wanted to confirm who these people were. We had no other intention. If our rash actions upset you, Great Hero Jeok…”

hunks.baseline: “You didn’t upset me. You just made an even bigger mess.”
hunks.sol: “They didn’t upset me. You made a far bigger mess than that.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang frowned at the Taeeul Merciless Sword, then let out a small sigh.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang frowned at him and let out a small sigh.

hunks.sol: “Save your apologies for the people you scared half to death.”

hunks.baseline: One man, who looked more or less all right, hurriedly waved his hands.
hunks.sol: He was right. Unlike the few who’d been quick enough to flee, the civilians still standing there were trembling. One man who looked somewhat less shaken than the others hurriedly waved his hands.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, it’s fine, sir. It all happened so suddenly that we were startled, but…”
hunks.sol: “Oh, it’s all right, sir. It happened so suddenly that we were startled, but…”

hunks.baseline: The man trailed off as he looked at the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword, then shifted his gaze to Jeok Cheongang and me.
hunks.sol: He glanced at the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword, letting the sentence trail off, then looked at Jeok Cheongang and me.

hunks.baseline: “Y-You’re… the heroes of the Murim Alliance, aren’t you?”
hunks.sol: “Y-You’re from the Murim Alliance, aren’t you? The heroes?”

hunks.baseline: It was hard to call ourselves heroes after causing such a commotion, but I nodded anyway. The man’s expression—and those of the civilians around him—softened at once.
hunks.sol: Calling ourselves heroes after the commotion we’d caused was embarrassing, but I nodded. The man relaxed, and so did the civilians around him.

hunks.baseline: “The Murim Alliance… Isn’t that the place fighting those wicked foreign invaders?”
hunks.sol: “The Murim Alliance… Isn’t that the group fighting those wicked foreign invaders?”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. There seems to have been a little misunderstanding.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. There’s been a little misunderstanding.”

hunks.baseline: “Damn it. I thought we were done for.”
hunks.sol: “Damn it. I thought we were going to die.”

hunks.baseline: Just as sighs of relief rose from all sides, the man who’d spoken first brightened and continued.
hunks.sol: Sighs of relief rose all around us. The first man’s face brightened, and he spoke again.

hunks.baseline: “To think you’re the heroes of the Murim Alliance we’ve heard so much about. What a relief. We saw a bunch of strange-looking people show up and thought they were the ones… Whoops. There I go, running my mouth again. Calling you strange-looking…”
hunks.sol: “To think you’re the Murim Alliance heroes we’ve heard so much about! What a relief. When we saw a bunch of strange fellows coming, we thought you were *them*… Oh, listen to me. Calling you strange fellows!”

hunks.baseline: Anyone could see they looked strange. More importantly, he’d said something else.
